Deliberately mapped rather than reused, unlike the four other STATO statistics terms. MOLSIM's sits under 'statistical analysis parameter' and is the confidence level a user SETS (e.g. 95%); STATO:0000561 sits under 'dimensionless ratio' -> 'ratio' -> 'statistic' and is a derived property (the proportion of intervals containing the true value). Input parameter vs derived statistic, so closeMatch rather than a replacement.

Mapped rather than reused. MOLSIM's term is scoped as an ANALYSIS ACTIVITY and sits under 'statistical test analysis' alongside its siblings; STATO:0000083 is the TEST itself, under 'goodness of fit statistical test' and OBI:0200000 data transformation. Retiring the MOLSIM term would pull a member out of a coherent analysis branch, so the correspondence is recorded instead.

Mapped rather than reused, unlike its sibling Spearman (which WAS reused as STATO:0000201). Two reasons the MOLSIM term is kept: STATO's label drops 'tau', which is less specific since Kendall has tau-a/tau-b/tau-c variants; and STATO's definition omits the concordant/discordant pair counting that actually defines the statistic and distinguishes it from Spearman's. Here MOLSIM states the concept better.

Mapped, not imported: SWO's term IRIs are http://www.ebi.ac.uk/swo/... , NOT OBO PURLs, so importing would put non-OBO IRIs in the release. NOTE the prefix: this term lives in SWO's 'interface' sub-namespace (http://www.ebi.ac.uk/swo/interface/SWO_9000054), so a plain SWO: prefix would resolve to the wrong IRI - OLS's obo_id field reports 'SWO:9000054' and is misleading here.

Mapped rather than reused because of a CATEGORY difference. MOLSIM places its helices under secondary structure > structural property > computed observable - a quantity you calculate from a trajectory (e.g. DSSP output, helix content). SO places its under polypeptide_secondary_structure > SO:0001070 polypeptide_structural_region, which MOLSIM already bridges under 'molecular entity' - a REGION of a thing. Reusing SO's term would move the concept across branches, from computed observable to molecular entity, add 5 SO classes, and strand '3-10 helix' as the only remaining child of MOLSIM's 'helix'. Both framings are valid; MOLSIM's fits how MD metadata records this.

PROCO frames it as 'a symmetry quality of a unit cell in three-dimensional space'; MOLSIM as a mathematical description of that symmetry. Same concept, slightly different framing.
PBPKO phrases it as amount of substance diffusing per unit area per unit time; MOLSIM as the rate at which particles spread by thermal motion. Same quantity.

closeMatch with caution: NCIt's definition is the DATED narrow sense - 'a microprocessor specifically designed for processing 3D graphics data'. MOLSIM's is the general-purpose compute sense (many cores for simultaneous operations), which is why GPUs matter in MD.

closeMatch because of a TYPE difference: MOLSIM models GenBank as a NAMED INDIVIDUAL (one specific database) while NCIt models it as a class - the same reason the PSI-MI database mappings use closeMatch. Note MOLSIM's definition is close to NCIt's wording, suggesting it was drawn from there.
closeMatch because of a TYPE difference: MOLSIM models UniProtKB as a NAMED INDIVIDUAL, NCIt as a class.

NCIt is the right source here rather than SO: SO has only SO:0001111 'beta_strand' ('a single length of polypeptide chain that FORMS PART OF a beta sheet'), not the sheet itself. MOLSIM's sibling helix terms were mapped to SO because SO does have those.
NCIt chosen over the two alternatives: CHMO's nearest term is 'X-ray diffraction' (CHMO:0000156), a different label and slightly different concept, and MI:0114 is scoped to interaction experiments.

Mapped to OBI rather than the NCIt match that surfaced (NCIT:C49291): OBI frames it as a DIMENSIONALITY REDUCTION, which is exactly MOLSIM's own parent ('dimensionality reduction technique'), whereas NCIt calls it 'a vector space transform'. OBI is also an OBO-registry source, which MOLSIM prefers.
